title: Mass Uprising Ousts General Ershad
reason: Ershad resigned 4 December 1990 (event says 6 December). Wikipedia and Swarthmore NV Database confirm 4 December. Year correct; date off by 2 days — minor discrepancy, not year-level.

title: BNP Victory and First Female Prime Minister
reason: Election 27 February 1991, BNP won 140 seats, Khaleda Zia sworn in as PM. All facts confirmed.

title: Devastating Cyclone Kills 138,000
reason: 29 April 1991, ~138,000 killed, 10 million homeless, landfall south of Chittagong. All key facts confirmed.

title: Twelfth Constitutional Amendment Restores Parliamentary System
reason: Referendum 15 September 1991, 84.38% in favour. Event states 'September 1991' and '84%' — confirmed. Passed unanimously in parliament on 6 August, referendum 15 September, Act on 18 September.

title: Opposition Hartal Campaign and Parliamentary Boycott
reason: Sustained hartal campaign from late 1993 into 1994, parliamentary boycott in early 1994. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Magura By-Election Rigging Allegations
reason: March 1994 Magura by-election rigging allegations confirmed as a catalyst for caretaker government demands.

title: Thirteenth Amendment Enshrines Caretaker Government System
reason: Thirteenth Amendment passed March 1996 after boycotted February 1996 poll. Confirmed.

title: Awami League Wins Election; Sheikh Hasina Becomes Prime Minister
reason: June 1996 election, Awami League won 146 seats, Sheikh Hasina became PM. Confirmed.

title: Ganges Water-Sharing Treaty with India
reason: Signed 12 December 1996, 30-year treaty, 35,000 cusec guarantee in alternate 10-day cycles March-May. All facts confirmed.

title: Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord
reason: Signed 2 December 1997 with PCJSS. All facts confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Floods Submerge Two-Thirds of the Country
reason: Event says 'over 75%' submerged; Wikipedia says over 75% flooded. ~1,000+ deaths, 30 million homeless, 700,000 ha crops destroyed all consistent with sources. Minor variation in exact figures across sources.

title: Export Processing Zone Expansion and RMG Growth
reason: By late 1990s RMG dominant export earner, ~75% of exports, 2+ million workers mostly women. General claim confirmed; specific numbers are approximate but within accepted ranges.

title: BNP Wins Landslide Election; Khaleda Zia Returns as PM
reason: October 2001 election, BNP-led alliance won 193 seats, AL won 62, Khaleda Zia returned as PM. Confirmed.

title: August 21 Grenade Attack on Awami League Rally
reason: 21 August 2004, 24 killed, 300+ wounded, Bangabandhu Avenue. Sheikh Hasina narrowly escaped. All facts confirmed.

title: Jama'atul Mujahideen Bangladesh Bomb Wave
reason: 17 August 2005, ~500 bombs in 63 of 64 districts, 2 killed. Leadership executed by 2007. All facts confirmed.

title: Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
reason: Nobel Committee states 94% of Grameen borrowers are women, not 95% as stated. More critically, the event says '95% women' — a minor numeric discrepancy, VERIFIED with note. However the category 'fiscal_policy_change' is irrelevant to verification. Actual borrower count confirmed as 'more than seven million'. VERIFIED with minor note on 94% vs 95%.

title: Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
reason: Nobel Peace Prize 2006 jointly to Yunus and Grameen Bank confirmed. 7 million+ borrowers confirmed. 94% women (event says 95%) — minor discrepancy only.

title: Military-Backed Caretaker Government Installed ('1/11')
reason: 11 January 2007, Fakhruddin Ahmed installed as chief adviser, state of emergency, both Hasina and Khaleda arrested under 'minus-two' formula. Elections held December 2008. All confirmed.

title: Cyclone Sidr Devastates the Southwest Coast
reason: Landfall 15 November 2007, 3,447 deaths, US$1.7 billion damage, Sundarbans absorbed surge. All facts confirmed.

title: Awami League Landslide and Return to Civilian Rule
reason: 29 December 2008 election, 80% turnout (some sources say highest ever), AL won 230 seats (grand alliance 263 total), Hasina PM January 2009. 80% described as 'highest in Bangladeshi history' — confirmed.

title: Bangladesh Rifles Mutiny and Pilkhana Massacre
reason: 25-26 February 2009, 57 army officers and 17 civilians killed (74 total). All facts confirmed.

title: Cyclone Aila Floods Coastal Districts
reason: 25 May 2009, at least 190 killed in Bangladesh (event says 339 across Bangladesh and India — combined toll). 1 million+ homeless. Minor note: 339 is Bangladesh+India combined figure; Bangladesh-only figure is ~190. Not year-off or materially wrong.

title: International Crimes Tribunal Established for 1971 War Crimes
reason: ICT established March 2010. Confirmed.

title: Fifteenth Amendment Abolishes Caretaker Government System
reason: Fifteenth Amendment passed June 2011, abolishing caretaker government system. BNP declared boycott. Confirmed.

title: Tazreen Fashions Fire Kills 117 Garment Workers
reason: 24 November 2012, at least 117 killed, 200+ injured, Ashulia. Confirmed.

title: Shahbag Protests Demand Execution of War Criminals
reason: 5 February 2013, Shahbag Square, demanding capital punishment for Abdul Quader Mollah (sentenced to life). Spread nationwide, led to tribunal law amendment. Confirmed.

title: Rana Plaza Building Collapse Kills 1,134
reason: 24 April 2013, official toll 1,132-1,134 (sources vary slightly). Event states 1,134 — within accepted range. 2,500 injured. Confirmed.

title: Jamaat-e-Islami Registration Cancelled by High Court
reason: 1 August 2013 High Court ruling cancelling Jamaat's registration confirmed.

title: Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety Signed
reason: May 2013 following Rana Plaza, 200+ brands signed. Covered 1,600+ factories by 2015. Confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Returns Hasina for Second Consecutive Term
reason: January 2014, BNP boycott, 153 of 300 seats uncontested, ~40% turnout (event says 39% — consistent). Confirmed.

title: Prolonged BNP Blockade and Political Violence
reason: January-March 2015 blockade, petrol-bomb attacks killing 100+ civilians. Confirmed.

title: Holey Artisan Bakery Terrorist Attack in Dhaka
reason: Event states '22 people killed — mostly foreign nationals including 7 Japanese, 7 Italians, and 3 Bangladeshis'. Wikipedia confirms 20 hostages killed (17 foreigners + 3 Bangladeshis) plus 2 police + 2 bakery staff + 5 terrorists = 29 total. Italian victims were 9, not 7. The '7 Italians' figure is materially wrong (correct: 9 Italians). Total hostage deaths 20, not 22.

title: Dhaka Metro Rail Project Launched
reason: Ground broken 26 June 2016 (event says 'June 2016'). JICA-financed. First section opened December 2022. Confirmed.

title: Rohingya Mass Exodus into Cox's Bazar
reason: Crackdown from 25 August 2017. Event says 655,000 fled 'within weeks'; UNHCR gives 700,000-745,000 over several months. 'Eventually exceeding 900,000' and 'over one million' total are consistent. Minor discrepancy in the initial wave figure (655k vs ~700k+) — not materially wrong.

title: Garment Sector Surpasses $28 Billion in Exports
reason: $28 billion in FY2016-17, world's second-largest exporter, 4 million workers, 80%+ women, 80%+ of exports. Broadly confirmed.

title: Awami League Wins Disputed 'Night-Before' Election
reason: December 2018, AL near-total victory, widespread ballot-stuffing allegations, BNP rejection. Confirmed.

title: Road Safety Protests and Student Movement
reason: Protests started 29 July 2018 after two students killed at Shaheed Ramiz Uddin Cantonment College (event says 'Shaheed Ramiz Uddin School' — official name is 'Cantonment College'). Minor name discrepancy only. Confirmed.

title: Digital Security Act Enacted
reason: DSA came into force October 2018, used aggressively 2019+. Event year is 2019 but notes 'came into force in October 2018' in description — internally consistent. Confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Triggers Garment Export Collapse
reason: First cases March 2020, $3.18 billion orders cancelled, $500 million bailout. Confirmed.

title: Cyclone Amphan Causes $1.5 Billion in Damage
reason: Event claims US$1.5 billion damage in Bangladesh and 'at least 20 people killed'. Wikipedia and ReliefWeb put Bangladesh damage at USD 131 million, not $1.5 billion. The $1.5 billion figure applies to combined India+Bangladesh damage. Bangladesh-specific damage was ~$131 million. Materially wrong figure attributed specifically to Bangladesh.

title: Bangladesh Celebrates 50 Years of Independence
reason: March 2021 golden jubilee confirmed. Poverty rate and gender parity claims are broadly consistent with development data.

title: Protests Over Modi Visit Turn Deadly
reason: March 2021, Hefazat-e-Islam protests, 14-17 deaths (event says 'at least 17'). Deaths in Chittagong and Brahmanbaria confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Padma Bridge Inaugurated
reason: Inaugurated 25 June 2022, 6.15 km, cost 30,193 crore taka (~$3-4 billion). Event says '$3 billion' — slightly low vs some sources citing $3.6-4B, but within acceptable range. Connects 21 southwestern districts claim broadly consistent. Confirmed.

title: Foreign Exchange Reserve Crisis and IMF Bailout Talks
reason: Reserves fell from ~$46B to below $34B in 2022, import restrictions, IMF $4.7B application confirmed.

title: Dhaka Metro Rail First Section Opens
reason: Inaugurated 28 December 2022, public service from 29 December, Uttara North to Agargaon. Confirmed.

title: IMF $4.7 Billion Loan Approved amid Macroeconomic Stress
reason: Approved January 30-31 2023, $4.7 billion ECF. Taka depreciation 25%+ confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Student Quota Protests and Downfall of Sheikh Hasina
reason: July 2024 protests against 30% freedom-fighter quota reinstatement. Hasina resigned and fled 5 August 2024. ~300+ killed in crackdown. Confirmed.

title: Muhammad Yunus Heads Interim Government
reason: Sworn in 8 August 2024 as chief adviser. Confirmed.

title: Rohingya Camp Violence and Security Deterioration
reason: Escalating ARSA-linked violence in Cox's Bazar camps 2024-2025, population approaching 1.2 million. Consistent with known conditions.

title: Female Garment Workers Gain Economic Agency
reason: By mid-1990s ~2 million women in garment factories, highest female industrial employment in South Asia. Documented empowerment effects. Confirmed.

title: Dhakaâ€“Chittagong Highway Expansion
reason: ADB co-financed four-lane expansion of Dhaka-Chittagong corridor, substantially completed 2003-2005. Confirmed.

title: Bangladesh Achieves Major MDG Gains in Child Mortality
reason: Rapid child mortality decline from ~150 per 1,000 in 1990 to under 80 by 2000. ORT, immunisation, NGO networks cited. Confirmed.

title: LDC Graduation Scheduled: Bangladesh to Exit Least Developed Country Status
reason: Scheduled graduation November 2026 confirmed (Bangladesh requested extension in February 2026 but this is a post-curation development). ~$8 billion trade preference loss estimate consistent with sources. Confirmed.
